decisive_items: skin biopsy showed orthokeratosis with rare lymphocytes at dermal/epidermal junction, minimal basal vacuolar change, pigment incontinence, and diffuse vasculopathy with fibrin thrombi in deep dermal vessels
response.rationale: SLE is the best fit: symmetric arthritis, lymphocytopenia, positive anti-SSA and anticardiolipin, and interface dermatitis with vasculopathy on biopsy. Dermatomyositis is excluded by normal muscle strength and depressed CK; primary APS is unlikely without thrombosis and with negative lupus anticoagulant/anti-β2-glycoprotein; Sjögren's lacks sicca symptoms; ILD is a manifestation, not a primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: No sicca symptoms; anti-SSA alone is insufficient and the systemic features point to SLE.
Only one anticardiolipin, no thrombosis, negative lupus anticoagulant and anti-β2-glycoprotein; likely secondary to SLE.
Interstitial lung disease is a manifestation of the underlying connective tissue disease, not a primary diagnosis.
Normal muscle strength, depressed creatine kinase, and negative anti-Mi-2 argue against dermatomyositis.
